title: new task via Mirror code only
hypothesis: After a common task-0 pretraining phase, a frozen shared backbone plus a small task-specific Mirror coordinate can add four aligned tasks while retaining prior skills with much less incremental inference and resume-state storage than rank-2 per-task LoRA, without increasing task error materially. Arbitrary unrelated tasks should mark the point where private parameters are needed.
physical_object: One shared 16x8 linear backbone pretrained on task 0 and then frozen for code-only, LoRA, hypernetwork, and hard-tie methods
mirror_coordinate: One learned float32 Givens angle on the first input-coordinate pair per task; previous task codes freeze after acquisition
logical_multiplicity: Five task-conditioned linear predictors sharing one frozen physical backbone
targeted_literature: Infinite-Parameter LLMs: Generating and Adapting Weights from Live Data (arXiv:2609.18842)
Neural Subspace Reallocation: Continual Learning as Retrieval-Based Subspace Memory Management (arXiv:2606.30067)
InduceKV: Fixed-Footprint Continual Adaptation of Multimodal LLMs via Inducing KV Memories (arXiv:2607.02010)
controls: per-task rank-2 LoRA adapters on a frozen backbone
shared hypernetwork generating per-task rank-2 adapters
hard-tied frozen backbone with no task-specific state
independent full per-task weights as upper control
task_stream: Five tasks in sequence. Task 0 pretrains one common backbone for 600 updates. Four subsequent tasks each receive 300 AdamW updates on 64-example minibatches. Aligned teachers apply distinct Givens input views to the same task-0 linear map; unrelated teachers use independent role matrices. Task ID is supplied at inference and charged as one byte per task index in serialized manifests.

development.selection_metric: mean final held-out task MSE across all methods and both task families, with retention and bytes as preregistered tie-breakers

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes and actual serialized resumable training checkpoint bytes
storage.inference_serialization: deterministic packed binary records containing method, dimensions, every field name/dtype/shape, and raw tensor bytes; task IDs are stored as uint8
storage.resume_serialization: torch.save checkpoint containing complete inference state plus optimizer state
report_separately: total inference bytes after each task
total resume checkpoint bytes after each task
paid_objects: optimizer moments and step state for resume bytes

success_gate: On all three fresh aligned worlds, Mirror final mean task MSE <=1.10x per-task rank-2 LoRA, mean increase in earlier-task MSE after each subsequent task <=0.01 absolute, and incremental inference bytes per skill <=0.25x LoRA. Compare against hypernetwork-generated LoRA at actual total bytes and compute; if it matches, do not claim Mirror-specific advantage.
failure_gate: Both development seeds miss either Mirror's <=1.10x LoRA final quality or <=0.25x LoRA incremental inference-byte gate. Keep fresh worlds sealed after failure.

amendments.change: Inference payloads use a deterministic packed binary tensor-record codec rather than torch.save state dictionaries. The codec stores every field name, dtype, shape, raw tensor byte, task ID and method/shape header. Resumable optimizer checkpoints remain torch.save and are measured separately.
amendments.reason: Initial development at LR 0.003 showed generic torch.save container overhead dominated the very small Mirror code and produced 0.50x LoRA incremental bytes. A compact inference format better measures the deployed parameter payload while still charging all tensor and metadata bytes. The initial run is retained as diagnostic-only; both learning rates are rerun under A1 before any fresh access.

amendments.change: Compute shared-backbone bytes by serializing the baseline records with the exact inference codec; compute incremental resume bytes by subtracting a baseline checkpoint serialized by the same torch.save envelope.
amendments.reason: The first A1 development run subtracted a torch.save base size from a compact-codec payload, creating invalid negative deltas. Fresh data remain unopened. Development rows are rerun with matched serializers.

boundaries: Synthetic linear regression, five known task IDs
Aligned tasks share the same Givens orbit; unrelated task matrices are the private-capacity boundary
Fixed update schedule, not converged capacity frontier
No language-model, user-memory, or real continual-learning dataset claim
Optimizer state is charged to resume bytes but not inference payload bytes
